column1: # The kernel's compile-time test hooks (kernel/Cargo.toml features named as
# a smoke, canary, probe, ... that no Kconfig symbol owns): what a build
# selection may still add by name (tools/build/kconfig_to_cargo.py --select). F6
# moves each `pending` one to a runtime name armed by the kernel command line
# (`canary=`, kernel/src/canary_rt.rs), so its row boots the base row's kernel
# instead of building one; the target is about 40 compile-time features left.
# The classes that stay compile-time (tools/lint/kconfig_lint.py HOOK_CLASSES):
# `const` (the canary changes a constant an asm block or a const item takes),
# `secure-boot` (its kernel enforces secure boot, where canary= is compiled
# out), `host-shared` (a host-test crate builds the same source with the same
# `hot`: a site on the trap, interrupt, syscall, IPC, context-switch, TLB or
# allocator path, where a runtime `canary!` costs on every pass: one load, one
# bit test and a branch (3 instructions on riscv64), against a null syscall
# and an IPC round trip of about 1,933 (riscv64, Chain E: 0.16 % a
# site); a cargo feature compiles to nothing. Each such line names the path. tools/lint/kconfig_lint.py checks this list against
